title: Evaluating the effect of automated insulin pumps on pain levels in people with diabetes-related nerve damage
official: Pain Alleviation In diabetic Neuropathy using hybrid cLosEd Loop inSulin pumpS: the PAINLESS study
summary:
Background and study aims
Many people with diabetes develop diabetic peripheral neuropathy, which is nerve damage related to diabetes that usually starts in the feet. For about a third of these people, the condition can be very painful. Current medications often do not work well or have side effects, meaning the condition can lead to people struggling with poor sleep and mental health. Recent research suggests that swings in glucose levels, in addition to average high glucose levels, can lead to the development of this pain. Hybrid closed loop insulin pumps, sometimes known as an 'artificial pancreas', automatically adjust insulin levels based on the glucose readings from a sensor in real-time. They have been shown to reduce the changes in glucose levels. This study aims to see if starting hybrid closed loop insulin pumps leads to a change in the daily pain of people with diabetic painful neuropathy. 

Who can participate?
People who have had type 1 diabetes for more than 5 years and have had daily pain from diabetes-related nerve damage for at least 3 months. 

What does the study involve?
At the start of the study, participants will be asked to attend a clinical visit to be asked questions about their medical history and have a clinical examination. They will then be asked to fill out pain and sleep diaries for 4 weeks. This is followed by two 12-week periods where two different treatments are tried. One will be continuing on their usual diabetes treatment. The second is starting a hybrid closed loop system (the Tandem T:SlimX2) and using it for 12 weeks. The order of these two treatments will be randomly allocated. During the study, participants will also be asked to wear a glucose sensor, and use activity and sleep trackers. At the end of each treatment period, participants will be asked to attend in-person for repeat tests, and they will be asked to fill in pain and sleep diaries. In total, the length of the study for each person is around 32 weeks. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Each participant will receive a thorough check of their condition by more comprehensive checks than are used in normal clinical practice. They will also be given the opportunity to use the hybrid closed loop system before it is more widely available. Study visits and completing questionnaires can be time consuming. No major side effects are expected from either treatment arms but when switching between treatments, participants may experience changes in glucose levels.

Where is the study run from?
The study is being led by the University of Sheffield. The Royal Hallamshire Hospital at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, and the Leicester Diabetes Centre at University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust are the two clinical sites where study activities will take place. 

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
February 2026 to February 2028

Who is funding the study?
The study is being funded by TANDEM diabetes, the manufacturer of the hybrid closed loop pumps that will be used in the study. 

Who is the main contact?
Dr Dinesh Selvarajah, d.selvarajah@sheffield.ac.uk

interventions.name: Hybrid closed loop (HCL) and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Clinical diagnosis of type 1 diabetes for at least 5 years (commenced on insulin treatment within 1 year of diagnosis)
2. Daily neuropathic pain for at least 3 months
3. Distal symmetrical polyneuropathy confirmed by the Toronto Clinical Neuropathy Score >5
4. 24-hr average pain score >4 (BPI-MSF)
5. HbA1c between 6.5 and 13%
6. On stable neuropathic pain medications for the past 3 months
7. Mean total pain intensity of at least 4 on an 11-point numeric rating scale (NRS; with 0 being ‘no pain’ and 10 ‘worst pain imaginable’) during the last week of the screening period
8. Willing and able to comply with the study schedule and be available for the treatment duration
9. Able to give written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Non-diabetic neuropathies
2. Other chronic pain disorders are more severe than painful diabetic neuropathy
3. History of major psychiatric disorders
4. Pregnancy/breastfeeding or planning pregnancy during the course of the study
5. Hearing or visual impairment, which would impede the ability to use the technological interventions (as per PI discretion)
